newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SASOL WELCOMES S.AFRICAN FUEL LEVY CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: SASOL WELCOMES S.AFRICAN FUEL LEVY CHANGES.

text.p: Synthetic fuel producer Sasol Ltd said on Wednesday it was pleased that Finance Minister Trevor Manuel had reaffirmed an earlier cabinet decision on the phase-down of the floor price for tariff protection to synfuels.
"Sasol fully supports the minister's proposal to decrease the equalisation fund levy and to increase the fuel tax accordingly," the company said in a statement.

The decrease was made possible by the phasing down of the protection floor price over the past year, as well as a relatively firm world oil price. As a result, the equalisation fund has accumulated a high balance, allowing for a reuction in the levy.

The equalisation fund levy will be cut by four cents a litre for petrol and 2.5 cents a litre for diesel as from April 2, while the fuel levy will be increased by the same amounts. This would have no effect on the pump price of fuel.
Sasol added that the synthetic fuel industry had enjoyed no tariff protection since November 1996. The floor price is to be reduced further to $17 a barrel on July 1, 1997.
